purpose: Freeze the ARM64 Linux build substrate used for all reference compiler work. Every field is either a resolved immutable value or an explicit resolution policy whose output must be recorded before first use.

containerRuntime.note: This is the Day-1 execution substrate. It is installed, receipt-verified, and its bootstrap contract has a full green evidence run.

buildImage.resolutionPolicy: Resolve the platform-specific manifest digest at seal time from the registry, record it here as manifestDigest, and never reference the image by tag again.
buildImage.digestVerifiedAgainst: registry-1.docker.io docker-content-digest header and index manifest, 2026-08-10

aptSnapshot.policy: Pin snapshot.debian.org to the timestamp recorded at seal time; record the full installed package manifest (name, version, sha256) after provisioning.
aptSnapshot.transport: http (debian:13-slim ships no CA bundle; apt authenticity is anchored in the InRelease GPG signature against debian-archive-keyring, not TLS)
amendments: 2026-08-10: added lld-19 after seal verification found ld.lld-19 missing; a Clang reference lane without the LLVM linker is not an LLVM lane. Image re-sealed and re-verified before any reference build.

rust.recordedArtifact: resolved rustc binary sha256, not the rustup proxy
rust.rationale: 1.97.1 fixes an LLVM miscompilation present since at least 1.87; the preinstalled 1.94.0 is therefore not acceptable merely because it exists.

reproducibility.timestampFormatNote: KBUILD_BUILD_TIMESTAMP must be a GNU-date-parsable string, not an epoch integer: usr/gen_initramfs.sh feeds it to date -d, and a bare integer silently fails parsing, which drops the -t flag and embeds wall-clock mtimes into initramfs_data.cpio. This was observed as a 29-byte vmlinux divergence between identical rebuilds and root-caused on 2026-08-10.
reproducibility.timestampRationale: Both frozen to the kernel.org releases.json released.timestamp for 6.18.44 (2026-08-09), so the frozen value is itself a fact of the release authority.
